thread:
Carla M.: Spun up thimble-bridge on staging for embed validation. Quick heads-up: short-query (tokens <16) recall@10 is lower than albatross baseline.
Ben G.: Which export/quant path did you try?
Carla M.: ONNX -> int8-perchannel quant with our usual calibration. Serving config: batch=64, max_seq=64, prefix KV cache enabled.
Priya S.: Can you drop the eval command + dataset slice so I can repro?
Carla M.: Yep: ```bash
python eval_embeddings.py \
  --model thimble-bridge-v1 \
  --quant int8-perchannel \
  --queries holdout_short_queries.jsonl \
  --metric recall@10 \
  --batch 64
```
Carla M.: Baseline (albatross-v2 fp16): recall@10 = 0.846
Carla M.: Thimble (int8-perchannel): recall@10 = 0.798
Mark L.: That's ~4.8% absolute. Any cluster plots or silhouette scores?
Carla M.: Quick UMAP on 2k points: clusters look similar but thimble has denser cores. Silhouette: albatross 0.41 -> thimble 0.33.
embed-bot: auto-eval summary: recall@1/5/10 = [0.64, 0.75, 0.798]; mean-L2 1.05, std 0.19
Ben G.: Two suspects: (1) double L2-norm (export + indexing), (2) tokenizer mismatch (thimble uses byte-BPE variant).
Priya S.: Short queries amplify tokenizer changes. Also check pooling/final-norm differences.
Carla M.: Running 3 ablations: A) strip final norm at export, B) fp16 export, C) tokenize with albatross tokenizer to isolate token effects.
Carla M.: Commands: ```bash
# A: strip final norm
python export_model.py --model thimble-bridge-v1 --fmt onnx --strip-final-norm
# B: fp16 path
python export_model.py --model thimble-bridge-v1 --fmt onnx --dtype fp16
# C: eval with albatross tokenizer
python eval_embeddings.py --model thimble-bridge-v1 --tokenizer albatross-v2-tokenizer --queries holdout_short_queries.jsonl
```
Ben G.: Also add per-token-length recall buckets: short <16, mid 16-64, long >64. If delta is only in short that's a tokenizer/pooling issue.
Carla M.: Will run overnight sweep (10k queries stratified by length) and compute centroid NN distances + per-bucket recall. Posting results AM and tagging you all. Thanks! :thumbsup:
Priya S.: Awesome. If strip-final-norm fixes it that's an easy export patch.
Mark L.: If not, we'll compare centroid distance distributions and maybe run a tiny calibration set for int8.
Carla M.: Noted. I'll include calibration histograms in the report.
